title_original: ‘Possible Love’ director Lee Chang-dong, ‘Being Heumann’ star Ruth Madeley, ‘Wuthering Heights’ HODs among participating talent at Screen FYC London
excerpt_original: The director and star of Brazilian Oscar entry ‘Gugu’s World’ are also confirmed to participate.

blocks.alt: Possible Love, Being Heumann, Wuthering Heights, Gugu’s World

blocks.text: Source: Jamille Queiroz / Warner Bros / Apple / Joo Jae-bum / Netflix
The first batch of talent for Screen International and The Barbican’s ‘Screen FYC London’ event has been unveiled.

The inaugural edition, which is free to attend for all voters, will take place on December 8 at the Barbican and will feature panels focused on titles in this year’s awards race, and insightful industry discussions about global awards campaigning.

Talent participating includes Lee Chang-dong, director of South Korea’s international feature Oscar submission Possible Love ; Ruth Madeley, the star of Sian Heder’s Being Heumann ; Allan Deberton and Lazaro Ramos, the director and star of Brazil’s Oscar entry Gugu’s World ; and three members of the craft team behind Emerald Fennell’s Wuthering Heights – costume designer Jacqueline Durran, a two-time Oscar and Bafta winner; hair & make-up designer Sian Miller; and production designer Suzie Davies, a two-time Oscar and Bafta nominee.

This event is free to attend for all voting members of Bafta, Ampas, European Film Academy, The Golden Globe Foundation, London Film Critic’s Circle, and Guilds (Director, Producer, Writer, Crafts). It is also open to non-voters, with tickets available to purchase for Barbican members.

Apple Original Films’ Being Heumann is director/writer/producer Sian Heder’s follow-up to best picture winner Coda . It stars Madeley as disability rights activist Judith Heumann, with Academy Award nominee Mark Ruffalo, and the cast also includes Dylan O’Brien, Madeline Delp, Rob Delaney, Ray Fisher, Michael Patrick Thornton, Antwan Tolliver, Daniel Durant, Jon Beavers, Roberta Colindrez and Russell Harvard. Being Heumann had its world premiere in September as the opening night film of the Toronto International Film Festival.

Possible Love is the long-awaited seventh title from Lee, whose previous film Burning earned critical acclaim after its Cannes debut in 2018. Possible Love stars Jeon Do-yeon and Sul Kyung-gu and follows the intertwined relationship of two married couples. It won the Silver Lion Grand Jury prize at this year’s Venice Film Festival and is South Korea’s entry to the international feature Oscar race. Netflix has released the film worldwide.

Warner Bros’ Wuthering Heights is award-winning filmmaker Emerald Fennell’s visionary reinterpretation of Emily Brontë’s classic British novel, starring Margot Robbie and Jacob Elordi. Filmed in the UK, including on location in Yorkshire, Wuthering Heights grossed over £25m at the UK box office. As well as writing and directing, Fennell also produced alongside Margot Robbie and Josey McNamara of Lucky Chap. Speaking at the ‘Screen FYC London’ event will be costume designer Jacqueline Durran, hair & make-up artist Sian Miller and production designer Suzie Davies.

Brazil’s international feature Oscar entry Gugu’s World follows a boy with a football at his feet and a heart that doesn’t fit the lines drawn for him, watching the place where he feels whole, beginning to slip away. Ramos plays his father who has remarried and forged a new life for himself. The film is directed by Deberton, whose previous work includes the 2019 comedy drama Pacarrete , and first premiered in Berlin where it won the Generation Crystal Bear and grand jury prize.
For more information about ‘Screen FYC London’, please contact Scott Benfold .
